_source: Approximate values per 100 g raw edible portion, USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy). Shelf life and storage are typical household guidance.

apple.name: Apple
known_for: Good source of dietary fibre (pectin), mostly in the skin
Rich in polyphenol antioxidants such as quercetin
apple.storage: Refrigerate in the crisper drawer; keep away from bananas, as apples release ethylene that speeds ripening.
apple.shelf_life: 1-2 weeks at room temperature, 4-6 weeks refrigerated
apple.spoilage_signs: Soft brown patches, wrinkled skin, fermented smell, mould near the stem

banana.name: Banana
known_for: One of the richest everyday sources of potassium
Good source of vitamin B6 and quick energy
banana.storage: Keep at room temperature, away from other fruit. Refrigerating ripe bananas darkens the peel but keeps the flesh.
banana.shelf_life: 2-7 days at room temperature depending on ripeness
banana.spoilage_signs: Black, leaking peel, mushy flesh, fruit flies, sour or alcoholic smell

bitter_gourd.name: Bitter gourd
known_for: Very high in vitamin C for a vegetable
Good source of folate; traditionally used in diabetic diets
bitter_gourd.storage: Refrigerate unwashed in a paper bag or cloth; use within a few days.
bitter_gourd.spoilage_signs: Turns yellow-orange, soft and slimy spots, seeds turn red, shrivelled skin

capsicum.name: Capsicum (bell pepper)
known_for: Excellent source of vitamin C
Low in calories, provides vitamin B6 and vitamin K
capsicum.storage: Refrigerate whole and dry in the vegetable drawer; cut capsicum keeps 2-3 days in a closed box.
capsicum.spoilage_signs: Wrinkled, soft skin, dark sunken spots, white or black mould around the stem

orange.name: Orange
known_for: Rich in vitamin C (one orange covers most of a day's need)
Provides folate and flavonoids such as hesperidin
orange.storage: Room temperature for a few days, or refrigerate loose (not in a sealed bag) for longer.
orange.shelf_life: about 1 week at room temperature, 3-4 weeks refrigerated
orange.spoilage_signs: Soft, sunken areas, blue-green or white mould, sour fermented smell

tomato.name: Tomato
known_for: Main dietary source of the antioxidant lycopene (more available when cooked)
Provides vitamin C and potassium
tomato.storage: Ripen at room temperature, stem side down; refrigerate only once fully ripe.
tomato.shelf_life: 3-5 days ripe at room temperature, about 1 week more refrigerated
tomato.spoilage_signs: Wrinkled skin, leaking juice, dark soft spots, white or grey fuzzy mould

potato.name: Potato
known_for: High in potassium and complex carbohydrates
Good source of vitamin B6 and vitamin C
potato.storage: Store in a cool, dark, dry place with good ventilation; do not refrigerate or store next to onions.
potato.shelf_life: 2-4 weeks in a cool pantry, 2-3 months in root cellars
potato.spoilage_signs: Green patches (solanine), sprouting eyes, soft wrinkled texture, rotting foul smell

onion.name: Onion
known_for: Rich in quercetin and sulfur antioxidants
Prebiotic inulin for gut health
onion.storage: Keep in a cool, dry, ventilated basket; keep separate from potatoes.
onion.shelf_life: 2-4 weeks in a cool dry pantry
onion.spoilage_signs: Soft or mushy spots, black mold on outer layers, sprouting shoots, foul odor

mango.name: Mango
known_for: High in vitamins A and C
Rich in polyphenols including mangiferin
mango.storage: Ripen at room temperature; once ripe, refrigerate up to 5 days.
mango.shelf_life: 2-5 days at room temperature, up to 1 week refrigerated
mango.spoilage_signs: Large black sunken bruises, alcoholic or fermented odor, mushy texture, white mold

cucumber.name: Cucumber
known_for: Over 95% water, excellent for hydration
Contains cucurbitacins and antioxidants
cucumber.storage: Store in the crisper drawer wrapped loosely in paper towel; keep away from ethylene producers.
cucumber.spoilage_signs: Yellowing skin, slimy surface, soft and squishy ends, white mold

carrot.name: Carrot
known_for: Exceptional source of beta-carotene (provitamin A)
Supports eye and immune health
carrot.storage: Cut green tops off, keep in a plastic bag with paper towel in refrigerator crisper.
carrot.spoilage_signs: Rubbery or bendy texture, slimy dark spots, white fungal growth, rot

strawberry.name: Strawberry
known_for: Very high in vitamin C and anthocyanin pigments
Low glycemic index and calorie density
strawberry.storage: Do not wash until ready to eat; store in single layer in ventilated container in fridge.
strawberry.spoilage_signs: White or grey fuzzy mold (Botrytis), leaking juice, mushy discolored patches

lemon.name: Lemon
known_for: Rich in vitamin C and citric acid
Antibacterial and digestive aid
lemon.storage: Store in the refrigerator crisper in a sealed bag or airtight container for maximum freshness.
lemon.shelf_life: 1-2 weeks at room temperature, 3-4 weeks refrigerated
lemon.spoilage_signs: Hard, dried-out peel, green or blue fuzzy mold, mushy soft spots

grapes.name: Grapes
known_for: Contains resveratrol and powerful proanthocyanidins
Natural quick energy
grapes.storage: Store unwashed in their original perforated bag in the crisper drawer.
grapes.spoilage_signs: Brown or shrivelled berries, white fuzzy mold at stems, sour vinegary smell, detachment

bread.name: Bread
known_for: Carbohydrate staple providing daily energy
Fortified with B-complex vitamins and iron
bread.storage: Keep in a cool, dry breadbox or airtight container; avoid the fridge which accelerates staling.
bread.shelf_life: 3-5 days at room temperature, up to 3 months frozen
bread.spoilage_signs: Green, blue, or white fuzzy mold colonies (Penicillium), hard stale crumb, sour yeast odor

paneer_milk.name: Paneer & Dairy Milk
known_for: Rich source of milk protein (casein) and calcium
Essential building blocks for muscles and bones
paneer_milk.storage: Always keep refrigerated below 4°C. Submerge paneer block in fresh water changed daily.
paneer_milk.spoilage_signs: Yellowing or pinkish discoloration, slimy surface, sour curdled smell, bitter taste
